notes: Audited actual results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, as reported to the RI Division of Municipal Finance under the state's uniform chart of accounts, not a budget.

Includes the town's appropriation to its schools ($27,824,623). Rhode Island school departments and regional school districts report separately, and state school aid goes to them directly, so total school spending is higher than shown.
Fire districts, water and sewer authorities and other independent districts are separate and not included.
Left out: other financing sources such as bond proceeds and transfers in ($890,677) and transfers out ($11,206,265), which are not new revenue or spending.

Retiree health benefits (OPEB) and the benefits, pension contributions, insurance and claims the town records under general government ($6,785,959 together) are spread across the town's own departments in proportion to their size, as in other states. Schools and debt service are left out of that spread.
Property tax is what the town collected (current and prior years' levies, interest and penalties). The FY 2024 levy was $86,016,956.
Debt outstanding is not reported to the state in a form that can be loaded, so fiscal health is not scored.

Political money counts PAC contributions, many from unions, to candidates for Newport offices (mayor or administrator, council, school committee and other town offices, placed by their filing address) and to Newport's party committees, filed with the Board of Elections since 2023. Corporate contributions to candidates are banned in Rhode Island. Individuals and party and candidate committee money are not counted. A filer keeps one account across offices, so local candidates who have also run for state office are left out.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.
